## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Jīvika Sutta* ("Lifestyle", Iti 91) is a canonical discourse situated in the third section of the *Itivuttaka* (It 3.42, PTS It 89). In this sutta, the Buddha examines the reasons why thoughtful individuals undertake the alms-seeking religious life, while highlighting the moral and spiritual dangers that confront practitioners if they neglect mental training.

Full parallels are preserved in the Chinese Buddhist canon as MĀ 140 (至邊) and T 765.94 (苦), alongside resembling parallels found in the *Piṇḍolya Sutta* (SN 22.80) and SĀ 272. The text's concluding verses have extensive passage-level parallels across early Buddhist literature, corresponding to Dhammapada 307 and 308, Iti 48 (*Āpāyika Sutta*), the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* (Pārājika 4), the Patna and Gāndhārī Dharmapadas, and multiple recensions of the *Udānavarga* (including Sanskrit and Tibetan versions) and Chinese *Fa ju jing* texts.

Direct discussions of the sutta in modern scholarly literature were not attested in the dossier; references to "Itivuttaka 91" in secondary citations invariably point to page 91 of the PTS edition, which covers the subsequent discourse, Iti 92.
